title: Jaissle wants Newcastle to build momentum off Arsenal draw
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutJaissle wants Newcastle to build momentum off Arsenal drawShareNewcastle United put in a strong performance against Arsenal last time out, and Matthias Jaissle wants to recreate that versus Brighton.Matthias Jaissle is hopeful Newcastle United can build on the momentum of their second half against Arsenal when they travel to Brighton in the Premier League.

Newcastle struggled in the first half against the reigning champions but came from behind to lead after a much-improved performance after the break, though they were pegged back by Noni Madueke's equaliser.
The Magpies have won just one of their last six league games (D2 L3) as they continue to work for consistency under Jaissle.
And with second-place Brighton, who happen to be the top scorers in the top-flight next up, Jaissle noted how important it is to pick up where they left off last time out.
"We need to be aware about their strengths and weaknesses," he said of Brighton.
"That's always our approach. We want to use the momentum from the second half against Arsenal.
"We will need to be smart, have good game management in certain aspects. Brighton have incredible quality at the moment, playing at a high level. They are a top team.
"Every game is so important. We can only focus on the next one. We are working hard on improving, creating more chances.
"Our aim and our goals are to perform [second-half against Arsenal] on a more frequent basis."
As for Brighton, they missed the chance to close the gap to Arsenal at the top of the table last weekend after a shock 2-0 loss to Hull City, which saw Oli McBurnie score two stoppage-time goals.
They remain six points off the summit and come into this match on the back of a big 4-0 win over Craiova in the Conference League, a game in which Femi Azeez made his Brighton debut.
"It felt great," he told BBC Radio Sussex. "It was a long time coming.
"I was just really happy to get on the pitch and to play in front of the fans. It was amazing.
"It was nice to be back out there with the boys. It was nice to touch the home soil for the first time as well. I can put the injury behind me now and just keep looking forward.
"I want to work hard, bide my time and take my opportunities as they come. Hopefully, I will become a main part of this team."
No Brighton player has been involved in more home Premier League goals this season than Diego Gomez (two goals, two assists).
The Paraguayan has either scored or assisted in all but one home game this season, the 1-1 draw with Leeds United.
William Osula has been involved in eight goals in his last 12 Premier League starts for Newcastle (six goals, two assists), including a goal against Brighton in May.
Of players with 1,000+ minutes for the Magpies, only five have a better goal involvement ratio than Osula (one every 125 minutes).
Brighton are unbeaten in all nine of their Premier League home games against Newcastle (W4 D5).
